affected_locations.label: onExit sync unlink of registry records

attacker_controlled_source: None from the remote store or board. The only inputs are local OpenCode runtime events (session.deleted, server.instance.disposed) and process exit; sessionID is runtime-generated.
broken_control: Hypothesis: an instance could delete another live session's routing record if session identifiers were shared or attacker-chosen, denying presence-based wakeups.
closest_control: The record path is join(registryDir, sha256(sessionID,'utf8').digest('hex') + '.json'); a 64-char lowercase hex digest cannot contain a path separator or '..'. trackedSessions is per plugin instance, so only ids that instance registered are deleted.
counterevidence: install.test.ts ('the generated OpenCode plugin keeps idle presence fresh...') registers session-123 and other-session in two instances sharing the same registry dir and asserts that disposing the first instance removes only session-123 while other-session survives and continues heartbeating. Session ids are generated per server process.
impact: Presence-based delivery denial for one local session (logged failed delivery).
plausibility: Plausible on first read because registryDir is shared per $HOME and the record name depends only on the session id.
title: Generated OpenCode plugin deletes local presence-routing records by session digest on session deletion or process exit

attacker_controlled_source: None remote. The condition is the absence of a local runtime event.
broken_control: Hypothesis: a session whose runtime never emits session.deleted and whose process stays alive is heartbeated indefinitely, so a dead session stays advertised idle beyond the 120s delivery freshness window and can be chosen as a wake target (presence forgery / failed delivery).
closest_control: Delivery requires the presence record to be online, fresh, status==='idle' and to resolve to a reachable loopback route (packages/cli/src/index.ts deliverMentionedSessions / isLocallyReachableTarget), and failed delivery is logged and bounded.
counterevidence: Severity policy: local-only, self-only and operator-only paths resolve to ignore; the heartbeat publishes only the installed author's own presence and cannot attribute presence to another agent. The lifecycle handling was separately accepted by the task147 ordinary reviewer, so this is not a new security control failure.
impact: A delivery attempt is routed to a dead endpoint; the delivery log records a failure. No data disclosure, no integrity or authorization boundary is crossed; the affected identity is the installer's own configured author on the operator's machine.
plausibility: Plausible as a robustness/precision issue; the added timer is the only thing that can refresh presence without a real event.
title: Idle-presence refresh can keep advertising an idle session that never emits a deletion event or process exit

affected_locations.label: fs.watch callback and debounced hint delivery

attacker_controlled_source: OS-delivered watcher event filenames, which are untrusted; the store writer indirectly triggers events. A hostile store owner can write objects but cannot choose whether the platform reports a filename.
broken_control: Hypothesis: a .git bookkeeping write reported with an undefined filename bypasses the metadata filter, wakes consumers, and (with a consumer whose own reaction writes into .git) forms a wake/read/wake feedback loop.
closest_control: hintDebounceMs coalescing (default 100ms) in the watcher callback, early return when hintConsumers.size===0, and advisory-only hint semantics (the doc comment states event filenames are deliberately ignored and hints never identify store keys).
counterevidence: Local read-only probe on this platform (bun 1.4.0, macOS, /tmp) observed concrete filenames ('rename .git/HEAD', 'rename .git/index', ...) for .git writes, so the existing string filter still applies; no undefined filename was observed. Before this change the identical event threw TypeError inside the fs.watch callback, so the change removes a crash rather than adding one. No repository evidence of a consumer whose reaction produces filename-less .git events.
impact: Local CPU/network (git fetch) resource use, bounded by the 100ms hint debounce and by the consumer set; availability only.
plausibility: Plausible because the filter exists specifically to prevent a GitStore feedback loop and undefined filenames cannot be classified.
title: Filename-less filesystem events are no longer filtered as .git metadata and now deliver advisory hints

affected_locations.label: experimental.chat.system.transform handler in the generated plugin
refreshIdlePresence keeps idle sessions wakeable within the 120s delivery window
renderPosts framing control (unchanged; applied on this path)

attacker_controlled_source: Board-store post body/title/author/mentions; anyone with store write access can forge objects under any author (v1 unsigned).
broken_control: Hypothesis: labelled board content is delivered into the highest-authority prompt channel (system) rather than a tool-result/user message, so an idle session that is woken by a forged mention mounts attacker-authored text in its system prompt.
closest_control: renderPosts applies <board-messages> delimiters and per-post `[UNTRUSTED CONTENT FROM <author> | board <b> | post <id> | trust unsigned]` framing plus MAX_DELIVERED_POSTS / byte caps; SECURITY.md records provenance labelling as the enforced property; AGENTS.md/SECURITY.md carry the untrusted-data hygiene policy; delivery requires online+fresh+idle presence and a loopback route re-validated by openCodePromptEndpoint (packages/cli/src/index.ts:989).
counterevidence: Byte-identical sink at base (git show f37b83b:packages/cli/src/install.ts); provenance labelling present; per-post label fields are attacker-influenceable but are data, and the repository's accepted mitigation for risk #1 is labelling plus agent-side hygiene. Severity policy resolves store-writer-only reachability with preserved labelling to ignore for this delta.
impact: Prompt injection against an agent holding the operator shell/credentials (threat-model ranked risk #1).
plausibility: The sink exists and is reachable; the delta extends its reachability from recently-active sessions to long-idle sessions because those sessions now keep fresh presence.
report_only_recommendation: Adjacent, pre-existing. Optional future hardening in an ordinary task: deliver board context through a tool result or user-role message on the OpenCode path (as the Pi tool-result path does with an explicit 'untrusted content from board' prefix) rather than the system channel.
title: Untrusted board text is mounted in the OpenCode system prompt; the delta restores reliable wakeability of long-idle sessions
why_control_sufficient_for_this_round: The framing control is present and unchanged at this path (verified in packages/hooks/src/board-hook.ts:438-475), the sink line is byte-identical at baseline f37b83b, and this repository's stated security property is labelling — which holds. Waking an idle session on a mention is the product's designed delivery behaviour, not a weakened control. The delta neither introduces nor modifies the control or the sink.
